guards.what: G1: C# resets the counter in THREE places (BeforeSideTurnStart, AfterRoomEntered, AfterCombatEnd) and the sim in ONE -- traced to the first reader, and safe
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 13's trace, executed rather than argued. The stale counter's only reader is `should_play_card` (velvet_choker.py:33), consulted from CombatState.play_card / auto_play_card / valid_actions -- i.e. only once the play phase is open. CombatState.__init__ runs `hooks.on_combat_start()` and then `player.start_turn()` back to back (combat.py:208-209), and start_turn fires on_player_turn_start at player.py:169, so the counter is 0 before any card can be played in the new combat. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b17.py choker): a relic instance carried out of combat 1 with the counter at 6 reads 0 at combat 2's turn 1 and its first play is accepted. THE ONE WINDOW THAT IS NOT SAFE, and why this is a divergence rather than faithful: a listener asking the hook from on_combat_start DOES see the stale value -- the probe registers a spy whose on_combat_start calls `hooks.should_play_card(strike)` with the counter forced to 6 and gets `False`, where C# would answer True because AfterRoomEntered has already zeroed it (CombatRoom.cs:228 fires strictly before Hook.BeforeCombatStart, CombatManager.cs:380-403). No ported content plays or previews a card from on_combat_start -- the four sim auto-play sites are powers.py:713, :1041, :3583 and enchantments.py:267, all turn-scoped or card-scoped -- so the window is empty today. Verdicted deliberate-divergence and NOT a gap because the observable is identical at every point today's content can look, and the port's chosen reset point (per turn) is the one the 6-cards-PER-TURN rule actually needs; flagged so that whoever adds combat-start card automation revisits it. Rule 7: combat.py, player.py, powers.py, enchantments.py, CombatRoom.cs and CombatManager.cs are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N3: an EXTRA player turn -- does the counter reset for it?
guards.rationale: Checked because the relic's cap is per TURN and an extra turn is the one turn boundary that skips the enemy side. C# increments PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber for the players taking the extra turn and fires the same SwitchSides path (CombatManager.cs:1404-1418), so BeforeSideTurnStart runs and the counter zeroes. The sim's extra-turn branch calls `self.player.start_turn()` (combat.py:650-652), which fires on_player_turn_start, so the counter zeroes there too. Both sides give the relic's owner a fresh 6-card budget on an extra turn. Rule 7: CombatManager.cs and combat.py are NOT hashed here.
